chapter_note: This chapter is dominated by later editorial/application material (notably in the second half: Mani-self reference, church/catechumen categories, exhortation). The oldest recoverable layer is a short cosmological-mythic sequence defining Envy as native to the worlds of darkness and narrating Matter’s envy against key cosmic/human figures (First Man; the Ambassador’s image; Adam). The opening contains a dialogue-frame attribution that must be stripped.

paragraphs.core_text: [The] entirety of envy is this first nature that occu[red] in the worlds of darkness.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue-frame attribution: “Once again the apostle speaks to his disciples:” (hagiographic/compilation frame marker; ‘apostle’ is Layer 2).
paragraphs.temporal_note: Opening frame formula signals compilation layer, but the remaining sentence is impersonal cosmological definition (Envy as a primal nature within the darkness-worlds).

paragraphs.core_text: In this envy that [ ... ] in it, the First Man [ ... ] its poiso[n ... ] its evil-doing. His garment[s] were [ ... ] it cut them and drew them; [ ... ]
paragraphs.temporal_note: Mythic-cosmological narration remains internal to the system (Matter/its envy acting upon the First Man and his garments), with no institutional address, exhortation, or citation formula.

paragraphs.core_text: ⟨p.179⟩ It envied the first image of the Ambassador, which he displayed to it in the heights abov[e], i[n] his form that it saw. It established the seal and the image of flesh, and put the impression of t[h]at image on flesh, its very own birth.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Cosmic actors and mechanisms (Ambassador’s image; sealing/imprinting flesh) are described as process within the mythic architecture; no shift toward church/polemic registers.

paragraphs.core_text: [The th]ird time it envied Adam, the fir[st hum]an. It seized a power from him, and bore it forth from a [rib of] of Adam's [flesh].
paragraphs.temporal_note: Although ‘Adam’ reflects the Manichaean Adam-myth with biblical resonances, the language here functions as internal cosmological anthropology (power seized from Adam’s flesh) rather than a Gospel/NT entry or ecclesial application.

Christian overlay vocabulary and motifs (‘blessed Christ’, ‘father of all the apostles’, ‘wood of the cross’) indicate entry through Mani’s Christian synthesis / later Christianized redaction rather than the older substrate.

Mani self-attribution (‘I myself was sent now, in this last generation’) plus institutional identifiers (‘my church’, ‘assembly’, ‘catechumens’) and direct address (‘it shall envy you’) mark a later applicatory/pastoral layer (also consistent with the chapter’s second-half fatigue drift).

Describes typical persecution dynamics against ‘the teacher’ and ‘the righteous elect person’ (community roles) and social slander among ‘mankind’; this is application to church life rather than cosmos→cosmos mapping.
Explicit temporal anchoring and institutional scope (‘until my time… to my church’) plus faith-fall language indicates editorial application to the community’s experience.
Exhortative ethics for ‘the wise person’ (steadfastness, hope, faith, standing firm in God) is pastoral admonition, not systematic cosmological exposition.
